learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic knowledge of the main steps that lead to the design of an industrial plant: feasibility study (product analysis, process analysis, technoeconomic assessment), layout analysis (material flows, connection between manufacturing and service activity, design of assembly lines), and fundamentals of service plant design (plant water distribution system, thermal energy production, piping).

Increase knowledge in the fields of industrial engineering with particular focus on the design of industrial plants, understanding the multidisciplinary context of engineering related to manufacturing and service plants.
Be able to assess the production and energy performance of industrial plants according to the application context.
Acquire fundamental knowledge of feasibility study of industrial plants, selection of product and of the production cycle.
Ability of carrying out techno-economic assessment of investment in the industrial sector.
Ability of designing service plant for the industrial sector.
Improve judgement autonomy, communication skills, and learning ability by solving complex problems related to the life cycle in the industry sector and by becoming aware of their knowledge.

syllabus_topics: Choice of the product and of the production cycle
Analysis of the production and exercise costs
Project management techniques: Gant, PERT and CPM

assessment_methods.method: Practical test (numerical exercises related to economic evaluation of investments, sizing of production systems and service plants)
Theory test (specific questions about selection, design and implementation criteria for industrial mechanical plants, production systems and service plants)

assessment_rules: The final mark is out of 30, with a possible "cum laude". The minimum passing grade is 18/30. A grade of 18/30 is awarded to students who can solve problems using course methods and criteria. A grade of 30/30 is assigned to students who demonstrate full independence in setting and properly solving problems, complete mastery of methods and criteria, correct language use, and adequate synthesis capacity.
